title: Telemetry-driven admin action shortcuts
creator: Alex Chen
description: Problem: First-line support spends significant time context-switching between alert pages, telemetry dashboards, and runbook docs to stitch together a safe remediation. We want to reduce mean time-to-remediate by surfacing verified, telemetry-aware action shortcuts directly in the admin console.
goals: 1) Surface high-confidence, telemetry-anchored action shortcuts on relevant console pages (incidents, model routes, dedicated pools). 2) Make each shortcut execute a small, idempotent task (a 'shortflow') that captures the exact check list / commands and logs provenance. 3) Ensure safety gating: RBAC checks, dry-run preview, and automatic rollback options.
acceptance_criteria: Shortcuts render on at least 3 console contexts (incident detail, model deploy page, dedicated pool health) with relevant telemetry snippets.
Each shortcut links to a shortflow that can be executed by an oncall with the proper role and emits a structured audit event.
Dry-run mode returns expected side-effect-free diff for a non-destructive action in developer environment.
Telemetry widget displays last 5 minutes of relevant metrics and the exact triggering signal used to surface the shortcut.
End-to-end trace recorded: console click -> shortflow execution -> action outcome -> telemetry update, visible in a new shortflow-run dashboard.
Performance: rendering shortcuts must add <50ms median to console load in canary region.
design_notes: We propose a lightweight 'shortflow' ABI: metadata (id, safety level, required roles), input schema, preview endpoint, execute endpoint, and an audit hook. Shortflows will be authored as YAML blobs stored in the admin config service and validated against a policy linter. The console will request contextual signals (alert id, route id, pool id) and the server will evaluate match rules to return candidate shortcuts. We must avoid embedding secrets; actions should call existing operator APIs rather than shelling out.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (canary): implement the shortflow schema, preview API, and a console card that shows 1-2 shortcuts for incident pages. Phase 2: wire execution with RBAC checks, audit events, and a simple rollback pattern. Phase 3: expand context matchers and create a shortflow authoring UI (design-led).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: accidental destructive actions. Mitigation: require a two-step confirmation, dry-run preview by default, and safety level classification on each shortflow. Risk: telemetry mismatch leading to incorrect suggestions. Mitigation: conservative heuristics for surfacing shortcuts and an opt-in canary for teams.
notes_on_telemetry: Candidate signals: error_rate spike, p90 latency increase, model OOM events, pool GPU utilization > 85%. Use combined heuristics (signal + metadata) to map to candidate shortflows. Telemetry snippets must be precomputed by the backend to avoid expensive client queries.
